reviews.title: Stays looking great while surviving life
reviews.body: I love it when I find something that looks exactly like I want it to and can also survive the chaos that comes with family and animals and living on a farm and all the rest of real life.  I loved how this rug looked in my bedroom when it was brand new, but the real test has been how well it survives life and the animals.  The cats are both black, shed terribly, and love to sleep on my white rug.  The dog got angry at me for having the audacity to leave the house for 90 minutes and went pee on it as a punishment.  Everyone else walks over it (it is a rug after all) with whatever is on their shoes and we live on a farm.  But this rug can stand up to all of it.  The trick is this:  wash it on the regular cycle in the washing machine with all your other laundry.  It doesn't shed all the fur.  Then dry it using the normal cycle in the dryer with all your other laundry.  Again, it doesn't shed all the fur.  That gets is clean.  But it looks sort of scraggly and ragged (see the first two pictures).  Then vacuum it very slowly.  I start in the middle and work in one direction, then turn it around and starting in the middle again work in the other direction.  The vacuuming fluffs the fibers and it literally looks brand new again (see last two pictures).  It's nice and thick and fluffy just like it was the day it arrived.  A white rug that didn't cost a fortune and can withstand animals and messy family and farm life and is restored to looking brand new by just washing and drying it with the regular laundry and vacuuming it?  Miraculous.  Ten stars.

reviews.title: Soft & fluffy but no padding whatsoever
reviews.body: Summary: Fun color that is true to the photo, soft & fluffy, but needs some under-padding if using on hard floorsI've been searching for weeks for a pair of (vivid, saturated, cool/blueish) purple bathroom rugs to add a joyful jolt of color to my grey-taupe master bath, to match some very nice towels I had found. Discovered that bath-rug prices had followed lumber prices into the stratosphere, and also found that few manufacturers made generously-sized rugs in deep, vibrant hues like the one for which I yearned. The few that I found were exorbitantly expensive. And I wasn't about to spend $80 for a pair of rugs that, pre-COVID, would have cost about $30 or so.Finally gave up searching for "bath rugs" and looked for alternatives. Enter these "muppet rugs."Color-wise, they're perfect. And, being so fuzzy & funky, they're also amusing - a funny little addition to an otherwise luxurious and "serious-looking" master bathroom lol. But, they have no padding whatsoever - the backing is extremely thin, like a flimsy animal hide. So, underfoot, they're surprisingly unpleasant to stand on. I plan to rectify that with a trip to a home-improvement or craft store where I'll get some dense foam-rubber, cut it to size, and place underneath these rugs (probably adhering with Gorilla tape or velcro to prevent slipping). That oughta do it...I hope.
